walkthroughs.body_html:
Innovation & Design — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Innovation & Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Innovation & Design.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 2005 Double Diamond models the design process?
options: IDEO
UK Design Council
Stanford d.school
Frog Design

options: SCAMPER
TRIZ
PMI
SWOT

mcqs.q: What is an iterative design process?
options: A cyclical process where designs are repeatedly tested, evaluated, and refined.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
A linear process from brief to final product.
A process used only for software.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ductility and malleability?
options: Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.
Ductility is being drawn into wires; malleability is being hammered into sheets.
They mean exactly the same thing.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.

mcqs.q: What is FEA used for in product design?
options: Final exam analysis of student designs.
A process used only for software.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
Simulating how a product will respond to forces, heat, or vibration before manufacture.
